channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Apple moves some iPhone Duo deliveries earlier ahead of Friday's launch
item.description: Some US and Japan buyers of the sold-out $1,999 foldable are seeing delivery estimates pulled forward by weeks.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4's campaign reviews land as it heads to Switch 2 too
item.description: Critics have weighed in on the campaign ahead of the October 23 launch, which includes a Nintendo Switch 2 version.

item.title: GTA VI is now one month from its November 19 release
item.description: Rockstar's long-delayed game is a month away, after slipping from 2025 and then from May 2026.

item.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is out on Netflix today
item.description: The 10-episode standalone sequel to the 2022 anime arrives on October 20, with Cyberpunk 2077 discounted 70% on Steam.

item.title: Street Fighter wins the weekend with $31 million and $51 million worldwide
item.description: Paramount's Street Fighter opened at No. 1 in North America and added $20.1 million from 65 overseas markets.

item.title: Nscale and Anthropic are reported to be in talks on a $45 billion compute deal
item.description: Bloomberg reports Nscale is negotiating a second deal with Anthropic for about 460 megawatts of computing from West Virginia.

item.title: Chip stocks bounce after their longest losing run in 16 years
item.description: Chipmakers rose on Monday after the semiconductor index fell 11% last week over doubts about AI spending.

item.title: Nathan Fielder's Holmes film opens to $15 million, a documentary near-record
item.description: A24's You Can See Everything took about $15 million from just 855 theaters, the second-best non-fiction opening ever.

item.title: Disney agrees to hire most of Character.AI's workforce
item.description: Disney will take on the majority of staff at Character.AI, the chatbot company that filed for bankruptcy this month.

item.title: SpaceX reports third-quarter results today, with AI spending in focus
item.description: Analysts expect revenue of almost $12.9 billion as SpaceX releases its second report since going public.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent is reported to share a seller's home address with a buyer
item.description: A Toronto creator says his Muse agent gave a Facebook Marketplace buyer his address and sent messages he did not know about.

item.title: Taika Waititi says his Star Wars film is 'very iced'
item.description: The director says the film announced in 2020 is on hold as he and writer Tony McNamara move to another project.

item.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund
item.description: Anthropic plans to put 5% of its equity into a fund for charity and AI job impacts, with more added as its value rises.

item.title: Steam Next Fest opens with a record 8,000-plus free demos
item.description: Valve's October demo festival lists more than 8,000 demos, about double June's event, with ArcheAge Chronicles leading early play.

item.title: Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation
item.description: Jim Keller's AI chip company more than doubled its valuation and will use the money to make more Galaxy servers.

item.title: Burger King Japan discloses a breach of 11.18 million customer records
item.description: Names, birth dates, contact details and order histories, mostly from app users, were exposed in early October.

item.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default model over Anthropic, its CEO says
item.description: The coding platform's chief executive says Replit now uses OpenAI's models by default instead of Anthropic's.

item.title: AI-made clone games are pushing indie developers to hide their demos
item.description: PC Gamer reports quick AI-built copies of new indie hits, with one studio cancelling its Steam demo for fear of clones.

item.title: Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl spends a 15th week at No. 1
item.description: Swift's album leads the Billboard 200 again, ahead of Olivia Rodrigo, Morgan Wallen, Ella Langley and Noah Kahan.

item.title: Sam Altman confirms OpenAI is building a humanoid robot
item.description: OpenAI's chief said the company will build a humanoid robot and expects a demo in 2027, with 27 robotics jobs listed.

item.title: DeepSeek is reported to plan training on Huawei chips by late 2026
item.description: The Information reports DeepSeek will pre-train a model on Huawei's Ascend 950DT, not Nvidia hardware.

item.title: Meta details Prometheus, its gigawatt-scale AI supercluster in Ohio
item.description: Meta's engineers say the New Albany site links hundreds of thousands of GPUs, aiming for about a million to train Muse models.

item.title: Nintendo says it underestimated demand for its Zelda Switch 2 console
item.description: A Nintendo executive apologised for shortages of the Zelda 40th Anniversary console and promised restocks, without a date.

item.title: People are using AI coding tools to strip ads from their smart TVs
item.description: Developers are using Claude Code and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to remove ads and tracking from Fire TV and Google TV devices.

item.title: PlayStation 6 memory alone is claimed to cost over $680 per console
item.description: An insider says RAM and storage costs could push the next PlayStation past $1,000, as AI data centers drive memory prices up.

item.title: 39 state attorneys general seek child-safety terms in any Character.AI sale
item.description: A coalition of states filed notice in Character.AI's bankruptcy, asking that child-safety and privacy protections follow its assets.

item.title: OpenCode says a breach may have exposed users' OpenAI and Anthropic keys
item.description: The AI coding tool says 1.4% of its Console users who linked outside providers may have had their API keys exposed.

item.title: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie will not follow the game's story
item.description: CD Projekt Red's co-CEO says the Paramount live-action film is set in the same world but is not an adaptation of the game's plot.

item.title: Tamil film composer Deva dies at 75
item.description: The composer and singer, who scored more than 400 films and pioneered gaana music in cinema, died in Chennai.

item.title: Dream Labs raises a $90 million seed round for robot foundation models
item.description: Founded this year by former Nvidia researchers, Dream Labs says its Dream-1 model controls robots from over 20 hardware makers.

item.title: New Macs are reported for November 6 as a new iPad mini case leaks
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says new Macs arrive November 6, and a filing for an unreleased iPad mini case hints at a redesign.

item.title: Nikkei discloses its third data breach in about a month
item.description: The Japanese media group says stolen credentials exposed about 1.83 million records from a development system.

item.title: Samsung is reported to use rival TSMC to make base dies for Nvidia's custom memory
item.description: Samsung will reportedly tap TSMC's 3nm process for the base die of Nvidia's custom HBM, its first such handoff.

item.title: ARC Raiders bounces back to 185,000 Steam players after its Frozen Trail update
item.description: Embark's shooter hit its highest Steam player count since March after a free update and a free-to-play week.

item.title: Valve prices the Steam Frame headset from $1,059
item.description: Valve's Steam Frame costs $1,059 with 256GB or $1,299 with 1TB, with reservation holders able to order by December or in 2027.

item.title: Nvidia's app now lets AI agents change your settings by default
item.description: An Nvidia App update lets AI agents adjust game graphics, recording and laptop modes without users opting in.

item.title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse debuts third in the UK charts
item.description: Konami's new Castlevania entered at No. 3 behind EA Sports FC 27 and newcomer Control Resonant.

item.title: Josh Hartnett's Below jumps to the top of Netflix's series chart
item.description: The six-part Newfoundland-set limited series climbed from 13th to first in What's on Netflix's weekly ranking.

item.title: Hack exposes data on about 7 million California public school students
item.description: A compromised login at testing provider Education Testing Service exposed names, addresses, demographics and disability status.

item.title: Konami's president says AI cannot replace the people behind great games
item.description: Hideki Hayakawa says generative AI will not change the games market much and that creators matter most.

item.title: Liquid Swords, the studio behind Samson, goes bankrupt
item.description: The Swedish studio founded by a former Just Cause director is bankrupt after months of unpaid wages, with about 30 jobs affected.

item.title: Whalefall opens fourth with $8 million
item.description: Disney's survival thriller took about $8 million in North America and $9.5 million overseas, short of expectations.

item.title: New Sense and Sensibility opens to $7.25 million with an A- CinemaScore
item.description: Focus Features' Jane Austen adaptation took an estimated $7.25 million from 2,545 theaters, with audiences rating it highly.

item.title: Sergei Loznitsa's Imperium wins Best Film at the London Film Festival
item.description: The archive documentary about the early-1970s Soviet Union took the top prize as the 70th BFI London Film Festival closed.
